newsitem.title: USA: Incstar to be bought by American Standard.
newsitem.headline: Incstar to be bought by American Standard.

text.p: Incstar Corp., a small manufacturer of clinical and medical tests, said Friday it has agreed to be acquired by American Standard Inc., a unit of American Standard Cos. Inc., for $105.5 million in cash.

Under the agreement, American Standard will offer $6.32 for each of Incstar's roughly 16.7 million shares outstanding. Incstar, based in Stillwater, Minn., will become part of a newly formed medical systems group within American Standard.
Incstar also said that Sorin Biomedica SpA, its majority shareholder, has a memorandum of understanding to sell Sorin's European diagnostics division to American Standard.
Sorin, an affiliate of Italy's Fiat SpA, owns about 53 percent of Incstar.
The companies have agreed to close both deals simultaneously.
Incstar had sales of $45.7 million in 1995, making it a small player in the $6 billion global market for products that test for disease in human blood, urine and other materials.
The market is dominated by giants like Abbott Laboratories Inc., Diagnostics Products Corp., Boehringer Mannheim Corp. and Baxter International Inc.
Incstar's stock rose $1.66 to $5.75 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
